title: Verstappen wins exhilarating Las Vegas Grand Prix
excerpt:
Max Verstappen has taken victory in a thrilling and frenetic Las Vegas Grand Prix, the four-time World Champion managing to hold off a race-long challenge from the Mercedes pair – who both dramatically fell back from the podium positions in the final laps – to seal his third win on the streets of Nevada ahead of the McLaren duo.

Verstappen had made a good start to lead from pole position when the race got underway – but with fine margins throughout the pack, the order continued to evolve as battles played out across the field, with George Russell frequently overtaking the Red Bull only for Verstappen to retake the position moments later.

The Dutchman also held onto P1 amid a Safety Car phase mid-race following a collision between Sergio Perez and Rafael Camara – and while Isack Hadjar dropped backwards after damaging his front wing, the fight continued amongst the leading cars as the event headed into its second half.

Despite the lead still changing hands multiple times – with Kimi Antonelli also getting involved – Verstappen continually grabbed it back, but question marks remained over whether he could do this to the final lap. However, the threat from Mercedes was nullified when Russell locked up and fell to ninth in the closing stages, while Antonelli appeared to suffer an issue that saw him slip down to fourth.

This meant that Verstappen claimed a stunning win ahead of the McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri. Antonelli had to settle for fourth, while Pierre Gasly and Franco Colapinto secured a solid points haul for Alpine in fifth and sixth respectively.

Lewis Hamilton was seventh for Ferrari in an eventful race for the Scuderia, the Briton having taken a 10-second time penalty for leaving the track and gaining an advantage in an earlier battle with Norris while he also made contact with team mate Charles Leclerc later on, for which the Monegasque received a 10-second penalty of his own.

Carlos Sainz scored for Williams with P8 in his 250th Grand Prix, while Russell and Leclerc were likely to be less happy in P9 and P10. The Audis of Nico Hulkenberg and Gabriel Bortoleto just missed out in 11th and 12th, as did Haas’ Ollie Bearman in 13th place.

Hadjar wound up in P14 on a disappointing day for the Red Bull racer, whose evening had started strongly in Las Vegas. An incident between Hadjar and Russell will be investigated after the race. It was also a tough outing for Racing Bulls, with Liam Lawson crossing the line in P15 after starting from the pit lane due to a fuel leak on his car.

Camara ended his second Grand Prix in 16th ahead of Lance Stroll in the Aston Martin and Cadillac’s Valtteri Bottas, while Fernando Alonso retired near the end of the event.

Arvid Lindblad was amongst the retirees after spinning his Racing Bulls machine behind the Safety Car, with Perez also unable to continue following his collision with Camara. Alex Albon, meanwhile, had been wheeled off the grid prior to the start and could not participate due to damage from overheating brakes.

AS IT HAPPENED

After an action-packed two days on track in Nevada, the attentions of the paddock turned to Saturday night’s 50-lap Las Vegas Grand Prix, for which Verstappen – a two-time winner of the event in previous years – would start from pole position.

While Antonelli had set the fastest time in the dying moments of Friday’s Qualifying, a five-place penalty due to a power unit change dropped the Italian down to P6 on the grid – meaning that Verstappen and Russell were promoted to the front row.

That did not mark the only change to the order, as other drivers also served their respective penalties. Piastri slipped from P7 to P17, while Sainz’s P14 in Qualifying ultimately became P20 and Stroll was demoted from P20 to P21. Bearman, meanwhile, did not set a competitive time due to his penalties putting him at the back of the order.

Heavy rain had affected running when the weekend began on Thursday, but dry and cool conditions looked to be in store as the grid started to assemble for the Grand Prix. One driver yet to make to his P7 slot as the start time neared, however, was Lawson, with Racing Bulls confirming that he would start the race from the pit lane following a fuel leak on the car.

Meanwhile there was also trouble for Albon, whose Williams was wheeled off the grid from P14 following an issue with the brakes overheating. The team subsequently confirmed that the Thai driver would not be able to race due to the damage sustained by the heat on the way to the grid.

When the rest of the field were in place and the tyre blankets had been removed, it was revealed that the majority of the pack would start on the soft compound with the exception of Antonelli, Lawson and Bearman on the medium.

After the formation lap had been completed and the five lights went out in Las Vegas, a strong launch for Verstappen saw the polesitter lead away from Russell, while behind them Hadjar tried to go around the outside of Norris in a fight for third before having to back down.

It did not take long for the Frenchman to find a way through, however, with the Red Bull utilising the power of the slipstream to overtake on the straight. Meanwhile Gasly had moved ahead of team mate Colapinto to go up to P6 and Hamilton was now in front of Leclerc following Ferrari’s tough Qualifying.

Russell surged ahead of Verstappen on Lap 2 but his time at the front was brief, with Verstappen sweeping ahead around the outside again at the final corner. Hadjar also looked to be getting involved with the battle and subsequently repeated Verstappen’s move on Russell – this time to the inside – one tour later to move into P2.

The scrap was far from over, however. Russell momentarily overtook again on Lap 4, only for Hadjar to quickly retake the position – and soon Lindblad and Norris had also joined the party, the Racing Bulls having also briefly moved ahead of Russell before the Mercedes retook the place.

Up ahead the lead was potentially changing hands too, with Hadjar going side-by-side alongside Verstappen – leading to the Frenchman being told over the radio to avoid losing time with the team due to the threat of Russell behind. The Silver Arrows machine had indeed closed up again moments later, with little to separate the pack.

“Can he stop defending? Because otherwise we’re just going to lose time,” Hadjar radioed in on Lap 8. Soon afterwards the French driver pulled alongside but did not overtake – but one tour later, Russell had made a move on Hadjar to split the Red Bulls.

By the Lap 10 mark, the order stood as Verstappen, Russell, Hadjar, Gasly, Lindblad, Norris, Antonelli, Hamilton, Leclerc and Piastri, the gaps remaining fine throughout the pack. Russell subsequently managed to grab the lead, only for Verstappen to snatch it back again moments later.

Elsewhere Antonelli had taken P5 while Norris was engaged in a close scrap with the Ferrari duo, the Briton ultimately losing out to both cars before also slipping backwards behind Colapinto and Piastri. The stewards went on to confirm that they would investigate Hamilton for leaving the track and gaining an advantage in the fight with Norris.

As another brief swap for the lead played out at the front – with Russell ahead for a moment before Verstappen retook the position – it looked as if the top five had slightly broken away. Gasly had managed to stay involved and engaged in a scrap with Hadjar for third, the Alpine driver enjoying a strong outing in Las Vegas.

Over at Ferrari, Leclerc – running behind Hamilton and Piastri – reported: “He needs to be careful with his squeezing because it’s not going to end well.” Hamilton was soon on the radio himself, asking his engineer if he could tell Leclerc to “back the **** off” as the Briton fought to keep Piastri at bay.

There was bad news for Hamilton moments later as the seven-time World Champion received a 10-second time penalty for leaving the track and gaining an advantage in his earlier fight with Norris. Meanwhile Hadjar had overtaken Russell for P2 – before the yellow flags were thrown due to Perez hitting the wall at Turns 14/15.

Replays showed that the Mexican had collided with the Haas of Camara, the latter continuing on while the Cadillac was out of the race. The Safety Car was deployed, leading to a flurry of action in the pit lane. Hamilton, however, was informed that he would be staying out due to the impact that his penalty would have had on a double stack.

Other teams did use the double stack, including Red Bull – with Russell feeling that Hadjar had backed the rest of the pack up in order to give Verstappen more of a breather ahead. Meanwhile Hamiton was brought into the pits one lap later, the Ferrari man voicing his annoyance at his penalty as he dropped out of the top 10.

There was heartbreak for Racing Bulls as Lindblad spun behind the Safety Car and was unable to get the car going again, putting the Briton out of the race. It marked a disappointing day for the squad, with Lawson running at the back of the order following his earlier fuel leak.

The stewards announced that the Perez and Camara collision would be investigated after the race as the rest of the pack continued to circulate behind the Safety Car, with the order on Lap 23 shaking out as Verstappen, Russell, Hadjar, Gasly, Antonelli, Norris, Leclerc, Bortoleto, Colapinto and Sainz.

As the Safety Car period came to an end on Lap 25 – with most drivers at the front now running the medium tyres, the exception being Antonelli, Bearman, Bottas, Camara and Lawson on the soft – Verstappen executed a solid restart to lead away.

There was drama behind just moments later, however, for the other Red Bull, as Hadjar suffered a broken front wing and dropped down the order. As the French driver headed to the pits – leaving him down in last place – Norris had moved up into P3 only for Gasly to snatch it back, while Russell was again trying to get ahead of Verstappen.

Once again the Briton pulled off an overtake, and while he initially managed to hold on through the last corner – the spot where Verstappen had frequently got back in front – the Red Bull ultimately returned to P1 later in the lap.

Hadjar’s day seemed to be going from bad to worse, with the stewards noting him for an unsafe release – though it was subsequently confirmed that there would be no further investigation. However, an incident involving Hadjar and Russell was set to be investigated after the race.

With Norris having moved ahead of Gasly for P3, the Alpine was then overtaken by Antonelli. Further back, the Ferrari pair were duelling over P7 on Lap 33, while the start of the next lap saw Norris slip ahead of Russell to slot into second place behind Verstappen.

Moments later the McLaren had briefly taken the lead – only for Verstappen to yet again grab P1 back. Meanwhile Piastri was now in fourth ahead of Antonelli and Hamilton had picked off Leclerc for sixth, with Gasly dropping back to eighth as the Alpine seemingly struggled with cooling issues.

The order rarely stayed in place for long as the laps ticked down. Antonelli had moved into the final podium position by Lap 37 – followed by Piastri and Norris – while Russell was again ahead of Verstappen, only for the Dutchman to retake P1 once again.

Further drama was in store as the Ferraris tangled behind, with Hamilton spinning and falling back to P10 while Leclerc was in P8. The incident was noted by the stewards.

In another intra-team scrap, Antonelli was now in front of Russell for P2 – and while the Italian then took the lead from Verstappen, the regular scenario unfolded of the Red Bull quickly returning to the front.

The pattern was causing some concern for Verstappen, however, due to the fact that the other car was generally ahead at the line before the Red Bull retook the lead into Turn 1 – meaning that he could in theory be overtaken on the last lap and not have time to grab P1 back into the first corner.

Over at McLaren – with Norris and Piastri now in third and fifth – Piastri was told to be careful around his team mate, leading the Australian to respond: ”Stop telling me to ******* be careful.” Meanwhile the Ferrari contact had resulted in a 10-second time penalty for Leclerc.

With only a few laps to go, Verstappen was still continuing to retake the lead from Antonelli whenever he was overtaken while Norris and Piastri were just behind Russell. The papaya battle was not settled, however, with Piastri taking P4 from his team mate.

Russell tried to move ahead of Antonelli on Lap 48, only to lock up and run into the barriers. While the Briton managed to reverse and get back into the race, the incident had dropped him down to ninth place.

There was further drama for Mercedes to come, with Antonelli appearing to suffer an issue as he fell behind the McLarens of Norris and Piastri in the closing stages – giving Verstappen some breathing room for perhaps the first time in the race.

As such, the Dutchman crossed the line to clinch his third – and arguably most eventful – victory at the Las Vegas Grand Prix with a margin of 0.639s, while the McLaren pair of Norris and Piastri secured a double podium for the team that perhaps would not have seemed likely a few hours earlier.

Antonelli settled for fourth, with Gasly managing the cooling issues on his Alpine to take P5 ahead of team mate Colapinto. Hamilton followed in seventh, while Sainz claimed some valuable points for Williams in eighth and Russell and Leclerc rounded out the top 10.

Hulkenberg, Bortoleto, Bearman, Hadjar, Lawson, Camara, Stroll and Bottas completed the classification, with Alonso retiring one lap before the finish. This brought the list of non-finishers to four, the Spaniard joining Lindblad, Perez and Albon.

Key quote

"Really, really surreal and something that I've never seen before in Formula 1 myself," Verstappen commented on the number of lead changes in the race. "I think in the beginning we had the deployment immediately correct, but of course people are learning and watching what you're doing. At one point, I couldn't get back into the lead before the start-finish line, so that's why I asked the question. But I think we had it set up well, and it was just a crazy amount of fighting. The slipstream was so big that it was just impossible to drive off, and it was crazy how many people were following."

What's next

title: Palmowski fends off Larsen for victory in Las Vegas
excerpt:
Alisha Palmowski converted her seventh pole position into her sixth and final race win of the season in the F1 ACADEMY Feature Race in Las Vegas.

The Red Bull Racing driver started on pole and held off a fast-paced Alba Larsen as the pair battled and traded the lead over the 13-lap race. Still, a late Safety Car ensured the F1 ACADEMY Champion took the win as the race finished under Safety Car conditions.

Larsen finished three-tenths behind Palmowski, with Nina Gademan rounding out the podium in third, securing second place in the Drivers’ Standings with a double podium for MP Motorsport.

Megan Bruce battled throughout the race but held on to fourth, while Emma Felbermayr had to settle for fifth and third in the Drivers’ Standings.

Wild Card driver Luna Fluxa Cross started in 12th, but by Lap 4 was running fourth after a superb drive, eventually crossing the line in sixth to secure points on her F1 ACADEMY debut. Jade Jacquet finished P7, with Ava Dobson in P8, after the American Express driver worked her way through the field from the back of the grid.

Top-placed rookie Payton Westcott crossed the line in ninth with an excellent recovery drive after being hit by Rafaela Ferreira at Turn 1 on the opening lap, with Mathilda Paatz taking the final point and rounding out the top 10.

title: Wolff reflects on impact of tow in Las Vegas Qualifying
excerpt:
Toto Wolff has explained how Mercedes learned about the effectiveness of the slipstream during Qualifying for the Las Vegas Grand Prix, with the Silver Arrows Team Principal believing George Russell had been ideally positioned to secure pole.

Mercedes enjoyed a strong session as Kimi Antonelli topped the timesheets ahead of Max Verstappen and Russell, but a five-place grid penalty for the Italian due to power unit changes means he will start sixth, promoting his team mate to the front row alongside the Dutchman.

The final stages of Qualifying saw drivers jostling for position to benefit from a tow along the circuit's lengthy straights, something Wolff explained had caught Mercedes by surprise.

"I've had 35 years in motorsport," Wolff told F1 TV. "I've never seen tows working when you're one and a half seconds behind each other like a train, because normally you should be penalised through the corners so much that the straights never compensate for it.

"But for whatever reason, here it seems to work. We found out later than some of the other teams, and I have no idea how these lap times came together."

Antonelli made the decision himself to drop to the back of the queue ahead of his final flying lap, with Mercedes initially concerned he wouldn't reach the line with enough time to start.

"We thought he wouldn't cross the line in time," Wolff explained. "But the truth is, even if he had, he would have been much too close to the car ahead of him, and so that lap for me was gone. And then, for whatever miracle reason, it was fast."

Speaking separately to Sky Sports F1, Wolff explained that he had expected Russell to be in contention for pole, although Mercedes still needed to investigate where the Briton had lost time.

"George, for me, had the perfect position. He was four seconds behind the car in front," Wolff said.

"We need to find out because I think there was something in Turns 7, 8 and 9, whether that was a mistake or something else happened. But it looked like the ideal position for a pole lap because he was quickest all the time."

Looking ahead to Russell starting alongside Verstappen, Wolff added: "Big cinema if they try to go through the first corners together. We shall be watching."

title: What are the tyre strategy options for the Las Vegas GP?
excerpt:
Kimi Antonelli was quickest in Qualifying but a five-place grid drop means Max Verstappen inherited pole position in Las Vegas, but will he be able to convert that to victory on Saturday night?

Running in FP3 – our only dry practice session – suggested Red Bull and McLaren, while substantially quicker than Mercedes through the twisty middle sector, are losing almost a second to the Silver Arrows on the straights. The tow hid that in Qualifying, but in the race, it’s the sort of deficit that can shake-out an order pretty quickly.

That is, of course, if the race goes by the numbers – and frankly, the Las Vegas Strip Circuit just isn’t that sort of track. While offering ample overtaking opportunities, it is also capricious: low-grip, omnipresent walls, and perfectly able to supply a game-changing Safety Car, VSC or red flag. Taking the jackpot in Vegas requires a quick car and a solid plan. The quick car alone won’t be good enough.

title: Charles Leclerc summoned by Ferrari boss after latest Lewis Hamilton aggression
excerpt:
Charles Leclerc was called to visit Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur before his media commitments at the Las Vegas Grand Prix after spinning Lewis Hamilton.

Leclerc hit the rear of his team-mate's car during the 50-lap race in Sin City, dropping the seven-time F1 drivers' champion down the order.

It also harmed his evening in Nevada, with Pierre Gasly and Franco Colapinto capitalising on the mistake and getting ahead.

Leclerc ultimately got back in front of the latter Alpine, taking the chequered flag in sixth. The 10-second time penalty he earned for the collision dropped him to P10.

Hamilton therefore finished in eighth after recovering slightly and being aided by George Russell's late-race error, which saw the Mercedes driver fall from the podium places to ninth.

However, after recent tensions at Ferrari over how Leclerc races against Hamilton, which were sparked by their clash in Mexico City, Vasseur wanted to speak to the Monegasque driver before his press duties.

Talks were held at the previous round in São Paulo to clear the air, but evidently they did not do the trick.

Both Leclerc and Hamilton had moved to quell the narrative after some choice words, particularly from the British driver, but that will be reignited now, despite the latter trying to prevent his team-mate being penalised for the indiscretion.

Speaking over team radio on the cool-down lap, Vasseur said: "Charles, I want to see you just after the race, before everything."

title: Max Verstappen ridicules shocking George Russell mistake after feud reignited
excerpt:
Max Verstappen has remained quiet on his feud with George Russell in Las Vegas, that was until Lap 48.

Max Verstappen could not resist a dig at George Russell over the team radio after the Mercedes driver went into the wall at Turn 3 during the Las Vegas Grand Prix, with the Dutchman's feud with the Briton having reignited just a day earlier.

Russell locked his brakes and clattered the barrier on lap 48 while trying to pass team-mate Kimi Antonelli, during a multi-car scrap for position that also involved Verstappen and the McLaren pair.

The Mercedes driver avoided serious damage and was able to reverse back onto the circuit, but the error cost him any hope of a podium finish, dropping him to ninth behind Lewis Hamilton.

Verstappen, who went on to win the race, did not hide his amusement over the radio.

"Haha well done. My god," the Red Bull driver said.

His race engineer responded in kind.

"Ok Max. Well he is still going," said Gianpiero Lambiase.

Driver

Why Verstappen and Russell are bumping heads again

The moment carried extra edge given what had unfolded less than 24 hours earlier.

Following a clash in final practice, Russell accused Verstappen of routinely compromising rivals' preparation without consequence, insisting that overtaking before starting a lap does not breach the regulations but that someone needed to stand up to the four-time champion rather than let him keep disrupting others on track.

It is the latest chapter in a rivalry stretching back to the 2023 Azerbaijan Grand Prix sprint, when contact between the pair damaged Verstappen's sidepod and sparked a confrontation in parc fermé.

Relations soured further at the 2024 Qatar Grand Prix, where Verstappen was handed a grid penalty for impeding Russell, and again at last year's Spanish Grand Prix, when Verstappen received a ten-second penalty for colliding with the Mercedes driver.

Russell will now look to put the Las Vegas weekend behind him before the championship heads to Qatar next weekend.

title: Lando Norris makes bold claim after 'chaotic' McLaren double podium
excerpt:
Lando Norris suggested the Las Vegas Grand Prix may have been the most "chaotic" race in F1 history after 35 lead changes under the lights in Sin City.

Norris managed to prevail as the Mercedes drivers faltered late on, taking second place behind winner Max Verstappen, with McLaren team-mate Oscar Piastri finishing third.

Yo-yo racing throughout meant the final result was far from certain, and so it proved, given the late drama in Nevada.

George Russell hit the wall on the penultimate lap, and Kimi Antonelli suffered battery deployment issues, dropping behind Pierre Gasly to fifth, before getting back past the Alpine.

"I think that must have been the most chaotic race ever in the history of Formula 1," Norris said following the 50-lap race.

"I didn't know what was happening half the time. I didn't know if I was going to have the best race and have a chance to win or end up last..."

Having started fourth, Norris, who initially looked to be in the hunt for a podium in the opening stages, dropped down the order to the lower reaches of the points with the McLaren's straight-line speed an obvious disadvantage.

However, when the race resumed after the safety car period, both he and Piastri found pace in the MCL40s, carving through the pack and back into contention.

"It had everything, this race," Norris added. "So it was tough. I timed things well in terms of getting back to the front.

"It was also a race not making mistakes, like a lot of people made. So fun day, chaotic but fun day, and a good result for us as a team."

title: Max Verstappen stunned by 'never before' drama in 'surreal' Las Vegas GP
excerpt:
Max Verstappen has claimed he has "never before" seen the overtaking and slipstreaming chaos which happened during his victory run at the Las Vegas Grand Prix.

From pole, Verstappen was at the head of the train of cars along the Las Vegas Strip, with the likes of George Russell and Isack Hadjar among those to yo-yo race with the Red Bull into Turn 14 and then on the final straight into Turn 1.

Late on, Russell's challenge evaporated after he locked up and hit the wall whilst trying to pass Antonelli for second, whilst Antonelli then suffered a de-rate to allow Verstappen clear air for the final lap.

The Red Bull then roared to his third victory in four Las Vegas Grands Prix, and his fourth win in the last six grands prix, and 75th of his career.

Reflecting on the chaotic race, Verstappen explained about the question he had asked engineer Tom Hart regarding final lap deployment after the yo-yo racing indicated a final lap blast to the flag.

"Not in Formula 1, that's for sure," Verstappen said when asked if he'd ever seen such a crazy race.

"It was really surreal and something I've never seen before in Formula 1 myself.

"In the beginning, we had the deployment immediately correct, but of course people are learning and watching what you are doing.

"At one point, I couldn't get back into the lead before the start-finish line, so that is why I asked the question [about final lap deployment].

"But I think we had it set up well, and it was a crazy amount of fighting, and the slipstream was so big that it was impossible to drive on and crazy how many people were following.

"Everyone is working really hard to still get these kinds of performances this year, and also of course still learning for next year.

"It was very exciting, I guess, for everyone to watch. I know, of course, it's a big show around here the whole weekend, and I hope that we delivered on track."

title: George Russell throws away potential win with Las Vegas GP error
excerpt:
George Russell was in contention for victory at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, only to put his Mercedes in the barriers on the penultimate lap in Nevada.

Russell fought Max Verstappen all the way from the start, engaging in prolonged yo-yo racing with the Red Bull driver, and stood a good chance of triumphing, but he fell out of contention on Lap 49 of 50.

Heading into Turn 5, with team-mate Kimi Antonelli also vying for position, the Briton made a mistake, sliding hopelessly into the wall on the outside of the corner, dropping down the order.

He recovered to ninth by the chequered flag, but his chances of clinching second in the F1 drivers' championship may have been done irreparable harm, with Verstappen winning his 75th career grand prix and taking 25 points.

Therefore, the gap now stands at 40 points with just two rounds and 50 points to go this season.

Antonelli suffered deployment issues on the final lap, dropping out of podium contention and leaving Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri to clinch second and third place, respectively.

title: Max Verstappen unstoppable as latest Ferrari intra-team clash steals Las Vegas headlines
excerpt:
Max Verstappen mastered 50 laps of pure chaos for victory in Las Vegas.

22 November 6:41AM

Max Verstappen delivered a pure masterclass in one of the most chaotic races in Formula 1 history to claim victory in the Las Vegas Grand Prix.

The drama lasted from the start to the very end, with Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri making it a double podium for McLaren after George Russell made a huge late mistake and Kimi Antonelli briefly lost power.

Antonelli did manage to finish fourth ahead of a superb effort from Pierre Gasly in fifth, while all eyes were once again on Ferrari, who suffered yet another intra-team collision.

Charles Leclerc spun Lewis Hamilton and received a 10-second time penalty, an identical punishment to the one Hamilton was also handed earlier in the race.

Max Verstappen unstoppable as latest Ferrari intra-team clash steals Las Vegas headlines

Results are being loaded...

There was drama before the race in Sin City even started, with Alex Albon being wheeled off the grid and failing to start due to overheating brakes. He was not alone in having pre-race issues, as a fuel leak saw Liam Lawson start a lap down.

As the lights went out, it was polesitter Max Verstappen who made the best start, although he did exchange the lead with George Russell across the opening couple of laps before overtaking chaos unfolded.

Due to the strength of the slipstream and battery depletion, the pack remained incredibly close, reminiscent of a Formula E peloton race. It became a Red Bull one-two on the third lap as Isack Hadjar passed Russell on the inside of the final corner, a hot spot for the Austrian marque.

The strength of Red Bull's powertrain was on full display, as Arvid Lindblad passed Lando Norris for fourth on lap four, with Pierre Gasly overtaking the 2025 world champion a lap later.

Lap nine, and Russell broke the Red Bull one-two by passing Hadjar, while Gasly overtook Lindblad for fourth on the following lap.

A critical moment occurred on Lap 12, as Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc both passed Norris, although the seven-time world champion cut a corner and received a 10-second time penalty for gaining an advantage off the circuit, leaving him absolutely furious.

Norris, on the same lap, dropped behind Oscar Piastri and Franco Colapinto, allowing the top six to break away.

The action remained frenetic, with Kimi Antonelli passing Gasly for fourth on Lap 17, while Lindblad also overtook the Alpine. At the front, two laps later, Hadjar got back past Russell for second.

Everything then stopped, as a safety car was required due to Sergio Perez crashing at the end of the long main straight in a failed overtaking attempt on Haas' Rafael Camara. It allowed everyone to pit, although Russell accused Hadjar of backing him up so Red Bull could double-stack.

Red Bull did double-stack, but Russell still managed to regain second in the pit lane. Ferrari pitted Hamilton a lap later to serve his penalty, dropping him to 14th. The safety car period was longer than expected due to Lindblad embarrassingly spinning while trying to warm up his tyres. It forced him out of the race.

© XPB Images

Ferrari turmoil once again; Verstappen victorious

Action finally resumed on Lap 26, with Hadjar's hopes of a podium ending after a front wing failure scattered debris across the circuit and forced him into the pits for repairs, dropping him to the back.

The crazy overtaking train started once again, featuring the top eight of Verstappen, Russell, Gasly, Norris, Antonelli, Leclerc, Piastri and Hamilton, who recovered well from his penalty. Just under three seconds split them all.

Unsurprisingly, the chaos quickly continued. Norris passed Gasly for third on Lap 31, while Piastri got ahead of Leclerc for sixth the following lap. Lap 33, and Piastri made another spot, this time on Gasly for fifth, who was passed by Antonelli for fourth moments before.

Hamilton's recovery from his penalty was continuing nicely as he passed his team-mate for seventh on Lap 34, before both Ferraris passed Gasly a lap later. Back to the front, and on Lap 37, Antonelli passed Norris for third, while Verstappen and Russell exchanged positions and then exchanged back again.

It was mind-boggling chaos everywhere, but it took a serious turn for the worst for Ferrari on Lap 38, as Leclerc spun Hamilton at Turn 7 while the Briton was trying to pass Piastri. Hamilton fell to 10th, and Leclerc received a 10-second time penalty.

The Ferrari drama handed Gasly sixth and created a five-way fight for the win between Verstappen, Antonelli, who passed Russell on Lap 39, and both McLarens.

Interestingly, Verstappen radioed to Red Bull that his energy deployment strategy had been figured out, resulting in him trying different strategies in the closing laps in preparation for a last-lap fight.

Lap 46 out of 50, and Hamilton passed Carlos Sainz for ninth. All eyes were on the fight for the win, although Russell's chances vanished on Lap 48. The Mercedes braked too late when trying to pass Antonelli at Turn 3, causing a lock-up and sending him into the barrier. Russell escaped damage and reversed out of the wall, but dropped to ninth, behind Hamilton.

The drama was not done there, as Antonelli suddenly lost power at the end of the penultimate lap, allowing both McLarens past and giving Verstappen a 1.2-second advantage – his biggest of the night.

To Verstappen's relief, it meant a relaxing final lap for the Dutchman, with Norris and Piastri completing the podium. Antonelli and Gasly finished fourth and fifth, with Colapinto, Hamilton, Sainz, Russell and Leclerc completing the top 10.

Sainz passed Russell at the final corner, while Leclerc's penalty dropped him from sixth to 10th.

title: 2026 F1 Las Vegas Grand Prix results
excerpt:
Max Verstappen prevailed in a closely fought Las Vegas Grand Prix, where yo-yo racing reigned supreme, where no one was able to break clear and take control.

Lando Norris finished second, with Oscar Piastri completing the podium in third, after a race that more accurately resembled a Formula E peloton-style event.

Kimi Antonelli and Pierre Gasly rounded out the top five in Sin City, in an incident-filled evening under the lights of the Las Vegas Strip Circuit.

Firstly, Lewis Hamilton earned a 10-second time penalty for going off track and gaining an advantage during an early-race fight for seventh with Lando Norris and Charles Leclerc.

Rafael Camara was spun by Sergio Perez, who retired as a result. It triggered a safety car, behind which Arvid Lindblad spun out.

The Racing Bulls driver had looked on for his best finish in F1, having been fighting in the top five, but dropped it on cold tyres.

Isack Hadjar had his evening ruined with a front wing failure soon after, tumbling down the order and out of podium contention.

But perhaps the highest drama came when Leclerc hit Hamilton, spinning his Ferrari team-mate around and earning his own 10-second time penalty.

But that was all before George Russell threw away any chance of victory by sliding into the barriers at Turn 5 of Lap 49 of 50.

title: Lewis Hamilton hit by Charles Leclerc to spark fresh Ferrari dilemma
excerpt:
Charles Leclerc hit Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton in the Las Vegas Grand Prix to spark a fresh team order dilemma for the team - and earn a 10-second time penalty.

On Lap 38 of 50, Hamilton initially attempted to move up the inside of Oscar Piastri's McLaren for fifth place at Turn 5, but backed out through the slow-speed section, with Leclerc then attempting to move up the inside of Turns 7 and 8.

However, he misjudged the move and thumped into Hamilton's SF-26, spinning the Briton around and down the order to 10th, whilst Leclerc is running seventh.

In a swift investigation, the stewards promptly handed Leclerc a 10-second penalty as Ferrari's team orders dilemma renews after their recent spats in Italy and Mexico City.

title: Isack Hadjar suffers dramatic wing explosion to wreck Las Vegas Grand Prix
excerpt:
Isack Hadjar suffered a bizarre front wing issue at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, essentially ruining his evening after a strong start to the 50-lap race in Nevada.

Hadjar had been fighting with Max Verstappen and George Russell out front, and looked well in contention for a second consecutive podium finish.

However, when the race resumed after the Rafael Camara-Sergio Perez-Arvid Lindblad safety car disruption on Lap 27, his front wing inexplicably exploded off his Red Bull.

He was called in to pit immediately with part of the wing stuck beneath his RB22 and having left debris strewn across the Las Vegas Strip Circuit on the run down to Turn 5. He emerged last of the remaining drivers, in P19.

The Frenchman was noted for an unsafe release during his first pit stop at the start of the safety car period, but the stewards declined to investigate.

However, the officials will take a closer look at an incident between him and Russell after the grand prix, potentially due to Hadjar backing up the pack whilst entering the pits for that stop, as Red Bull worked to double-stack Verstappen and the 21-year-old.

title: Sergio Perez collision brings rest to frantic Las Vegas Grand Prix
excerpt:
Sergio Perez hitting Rafael Camara at the end of the Las Vegas Strip has prompted a safety car to bring rest to a frantic race.

On Lap 18, Perez attempted to dive up the inside of the Haas of Camara into Turn 14, but misjudged and thumped into the left-rear of Camara, sending both cars into the barrier.

Camara was able to get the Haas going again, with the incident under investigation, whilst Perez retired on the spot with damage as the safety car was deployed for recovery purposes.

The incident will be investigated after the race by the stewards.

This brought to an end a frantic opening to the race where the leaders were yo-yo racing due to the powerful slipstream.

Max Verstappen and George Russell were central characters as they diced for the lead, with Isack Hadjar also involved, but was essentially told not to overtake Verstappen.

Under the safety car, the field pitted for the change to medium tyres, except Kimi Antonelli, who is on softs, whilst Lewis Hamilton served a 10-second time penalty for overtaking Lando Norris off-track.

Behind the safety car, Arvid Lindblad, who had been running as high as fourth in the early chaos, spun out, was unable to turn the Racing Bulls around, and so has retired.

title: Lewis Hamilton suffers huge penalty at Las Vegas Grand Prix
excerpt:
Lewis Hamilton has been handed a 10-second time penalty at the Las Vegas Grand Prix for leaving the track and gaining an advantage.

Fighting with Lando Norris and Charles Leclerc over seventh place in Nevada, Hamilton cut the Turn 7-8 chicane as the three cars jostled for position.

The seven-time F1 drivers' champion may argue he had nowhere to go, and with the yo-yo racing seen in the opening 20 laps of the 50-lap race, the opportunity to hand the places back to both the McLaren and his Ferrari team-mate was minimal.

Hamilton was running seventh, with Leclerc and Norris rising and falling across the three or four positions behind the 41-year-old.

Whilst 10 seconds may seem harsh at first glance, it is the standard penalty for such an incident, and because it was not on the first lap, the chances of it being mitigated were slim.

Rafael Camara and Sergio Perez's crash triggering a safety car made the punishment even more painful for Hamilton, who was unable to initially pit during the interruption as it would have hindered Leclerc behind him.

When race engineer Carlo Santi told him of the sanction, Hamilton exclaimed: "Ah, that's ******! If I turned in, we would have crashed!"

Therefore, he was brought in a lap later to change tyres and serve his punishment, dropping him down to P14.

Race engineer Carlo Santi told him of the sanction; Hamilton exclaimed: "Ah, that's ******! If I turned in, we would have crashed!"

And when informed of the damage to his race, the 106-time grand prix winner continued to be audibly unimpressed, saying: "That's unbelievable. Absolutely incredible."

title: Williams pledge investigation as DNS disaster strikes Alex Albon
excerpt:
Williams has pledged to investigate the cause of the damage sustained by Alex Albon - which has ruled him out of the Las Vegas Grand Prix.

Due to start in 14th place, Albon's machine was wheeled off the grid moments before the start of the race with overheating brakes.

However, the team were unable to fix the issue, meaning the Thai has posted his second Did Not Start of the season, following the Chinese GP.

It is also the fourth Did Not Start of Albon's career, following the 2022 Italian GP when he withdrew with appendicitis and the 2024 Sao Paulo GP when he crashed during Sunday morning's rearranged qualifying session.

"Alex will not race in today’s Las Vegas Grand Prix, as the heat damage sustained on the way to grid could not be repaired," said a team spokesperson.

"We are utterly disappointed for Alex to not be able to compete and will investigate the cause."

Liam Lawson also appeared to be unable to start with a fuel leak, but Racing Bulls managed to get his car going again as he started from the pit-lane.

title: F1 teams handed undercut warning for the Las Vegas Grand Prix
excerpt:
The Formula 1 teams have been warned that a potential strategy differentiator "will not pay" during the Las Vegas Grand Prix.

The possibility of the undercut can often prove a powerful tool during a race, but at the Las Vegas Strip Circuit, it almost certainly will not come into play.

That is because of the length of time it takes for Pirelli's rubber to warm up in the significantly cooler conditions compared to other circuits.

The temperature for the start of the race at 8 pm local time is likely to be around 10 to 12 degrees, far below that of many tracks.

Qualifying highlighted the fact that the drivers required two to three laps to get the tyres into a working window that would allow them to then go for a push lap.

Pirelli head Dario Marrafuschi, speaking to the media, including RacingNews365, said: "Temperatures are, of course, an issue.

"Cold temperatures and the working ranges of the compound are a combination that needs preparation of the tyres to find the proper grip.

"We saw during qualifying, and I don't have the numbers, but I think it was the highest mileage the teams have run in qualifying during the year.

"For this reason, this warm-up characteristic is also the reason that at this track the undercut will not pay. We don't think that undercut will be a strategy that you can use during the race."

[Article continues below]

Pirelli - 'Not a jump in the dark'

Marrafuschi has additionally made clear that a two-stop strategy is not really an option because of the time chasm between that and the ideal one-stop.

The Italian tyre manufacturer's simulations had initially indicated a difference of 14 seconds. After witnessing the running so far this weekend, that has been revised to six seconds, still highly significant.

Instead, the main dilemma facing the F1 team strategists centres on tyre choice around the one-stop, notably which rubber to opt for over the second stint, as starting on the soft is almost certain to dominate thinking.

Marrafuschi has confirmed that switching to the medium is the most preferable option, but then the hard compound, even though it has not been used at all by any team over the past two days, could be chosen.

"One-stop is the most likely strategy," he said. "In our view, soft and medium are the two favourite options.

"The second option is a soft-hard, but with the unknown that nobody has run the hard. Saying that, I don't think it's a jump in the dark using the hard, because we are at the end of the season and they all know the C3, and its characteristics. They've already run it on street circuits. It is an option to have a longer second stint.

"The window for soft-medium opens on lap 22; the window, potentially, for soft-hard opens on lap 21, only one lap before.

"For the record, though, I think it's going to probably be soft-medium."

title: Max Verstappen clash with George Russell triggers F1 fan disagreement with stewards
excerpt:
Max Verstappen was handed a warning for the near-miss with George Russel in FP3 at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, but F1 fans see things differently.

F1 fans have taken a different view from the Las Vegas Grand Prix stewards over who was at fault when Max Verstappen and George Russell made contact in final practice.

Verstappen was the driver under investigation after the pair touched at Turn 14. The Red Bull driver was ahead on the approach to the corner when he braked earlier than expected and changed direction under braking.

Russell moved left and tried to pass on the inside. The Mercedes driver had his front axle ahead of Verstappen’s mirror before the two cars made contact.

At the hearing, both drivers discussed the informal agreements that govern how they prepare for a flying lap. The stewards gave those agreements little weight.

What mattered to them was how the two cars had moved and where Russell was in relation to Verstappen.

After reviewing footage, telemetry and team radio, the stewards described Verstappen’s change of direction as "unpredictable" and issued him with a warning for erratic driving.
